## Deleted, with the evidence read (not grepped) for each

### 1. `captureAtomicTargetVersion` (was `:1084`) — whole function

`git grep captureAtomicTargetVersion` over the tracked tree returns exactly four hits: the three
function definitions themselves, plus one prose mention in `kaola-workflow/archive/issue-891/mission-list.md`
(a historical record, not code). Zero call sites. `git grep` was used rather than the local `grep`
precisely because the local `grep` is ugrep and skips dot-directories; a filesystem sweep naming
`.agents/ agents/ scripts/ plugins/ hooks/ templates/ commands/` explicitly returned nothing either.
(This worktree has no `.opencode*` / `.kimi*` directories at root — the dot entries are `.agents`,
`.env.example`, `.git`, `.gitignore`.)

### 2. The `else` branch of `atomicWriteSameDirectory` (was `:1154-1157`)

Read every call site rather than trusting a count. `atomicWriteSameDirectory` has **one** caller in
the whole tree: `copyAgentProfiles`, was `:1241`, now `:1170` —

    atomicWriteSameDirectory(target, fs.readFileSync(source));

Two arguments, so `expectedVersion` was always `undefined` and the `else` arm was unreachable. The
function is **not exported** (checked the `module.exports` object, was `:2958`): the CAS parameter
could not be reached from a test or any other module either.

### 3. `assertAtomicTarget`'s `if (expectedVersion !== undefined && current)` block (was `:1107-1113`)

Unreachable for the same reason: both of `assertAtomicTarget`'s call sites live inside
`atomicWriteSameDirectory` and forwarded its always-`undefined` third argument. One of those call
sites was itself the `else` branch removed above; the other (was `:1200`) is the live one.

### 4. `readAtomicTargetVersion` — whole function

Two callers, both in the rows above: `:1091` (inside `captureAtomicTargetVersion`) and `:1108`
(inside the CAS block of `assertAtomicTarget`). With both gone it has no reachable caller.

### 5. Consequential, and a judgment call worth flagging

The four items above cannot be removed cleanly while leaving the `expectedVersion` **parameter** in
place: with the `else` gone, `if (expectedVersion === undefined) { … }` is a tautology guarding an
always-`undefined` variable, and `expectedVersion === undefined ? 'atomic_stage_unsafe' :
'atomic_stage_conflict'` is a ternary with an unreachable arm. So the trailing `expectedVersion`
parameter was dropped from **both** `assertAtomicTarget` and `atomicWriteSameDirectory`, the `if`
was unwrapped (`let targetStat;` → `const targetStat = lstatIfPresent(destination);`), and the
ternary collapsed to its reachable arm, `'atomic_stage_unsafe'`.

**Positional-shift check (the hazard the brief named):** `expectedVersion` was the **last** parameter
of both functions, so removing it shifts no earlier argument. Neither function is exported, neither is
referenced via `arguments` or `Function.length` anywhere in the file (grepped `\barguments\b` — the
only hit is an unrelated comment at `:2826`). The sole surviving caller already passed two arguments.

### Correction to the issue's arithmetic (does not change the ruling)

Issue #894 says *"the `atomic_stage_conflict` code is also still thrown from six other sites."*
Measured per file, there were seven sites; six survive only if you count the four inside
`readAtomicTargetVersion` (`:1046`, `:1062`, `:1069`, `:1073`), which the issue's own table marks for
deletion, plus the `:1104` ternary arm. After the deletion the code throws from **one** site per file
(`:1866`). That is the correct outcome — the sentence's intent (do not rip the error code out of the
installer) is satisfied — but the "six" was double-counting the CAS half it was warning about.

## Verification

Verification tier: **regression-green** — full existing suite for these files green before AND after
a behaviour-preserving deletion, plus an executable equivalence/arming probe.

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `node scripts/test-install-model-rendering.js` | exit 0 — `Install model rendering tests passed` (17.1s) | exit 0 — `Install model rendering tests passed` |
| `node scripts/edition-sync.js --check` | exit 0 — `8 forge aggregator ports in parity with canonical.` / `committed kernel parity verified at HEAD.` | exit 0 — identical output |
| `node --check` on each of the three copies | n/a | OK ×3 |

### Three-copy consistency

The three copies were **byte-identical before** the edit (`md5 = b4f27cd6a3948f410a536af1593edf70` ×3),
so byte-identity is the relationship that had to be preserved. Confirmed byte-identical after
(`md5 = e77dc3e206d089e31e1eb8ff9c876c5e` ×3).

No sync tool owns this trio: `install-codex-agent-profiles.js` appears in neither `COMMON_SCRIPTS` nor
`BYTE_IDENTICAL_GROUPS` in `scripts/validate-script-sync.js`, and `scripts/edition-sync.js` never names
it (it is called out in `validate-script-sync.js:37` as *"Codex-only … not used by the Claude pack"*).
The canonical copy was edited and copied verbatim to the two forge copies; `git status` confirmed both
forge copies were unmodified immediately before the copy, so no concurrent agent's work was clobbered.

### Arming proof (a green suite is not proof a guard is armed)

Scratch probe at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ylpromax5-Workspace-Kaola-Workflow/f018e2ef-7526-4575-bcc6-e529af9f0e2f/scratchpad/894-probe-assert-armed.js`
(not a repo file). It hooks `fs.realpathSync(stage)` to swap the destination's inode in the window
between the initial `lstat` and the pre-rename check, then runs `copyAgentProfiles`. Run against the
**edited** copy and against the **pristine** `fa5157b3` copy in the main checkout:

    swap injected      : true
    threw              : true
    error.code         : atomic_stage_unsafe
    error.message      : atomic_stage_unsafe: atomic replacement target changed while staging: …/implementer.toml
    target preserved   : replaced by a racing writer
    leftover stages    : 0
    ARMED: assertAtomicTarget fired on the live path

Byte-for-byte the same verdict from both — same code, same message, same cleanup, exit 0 each. That is
simultaneously (a) proof the surviving guard is reachable and fires rather than passing vacuously, and
(b) an observational equivalence check that the deletion changed no live behaviour.

## Addendum — orchestrator constraint: no `edition-sync.js --write`

Received after the edit landed; already satisfied, no rework needed. `--write` was never run. The
three copies were kept consistent **by hand** (canonical edited, then copied verbatim to the two forge
copies after confirming via `git status` that both were unmodified), and the relationship was verified
with `md5`: byte-identical before (`b4f27cd6a3948f410a536af1593edf70` ×3), byte-identical after
(`e77dc3e206d089e31e1eb8ff9c876c5e` ×3). The only `edition-sync.js` invocations were the read-only
`--check`, three times, all exit 0.

**Nuance worth flagging for whoever does the central propagation:** `--check` reports *"committed
kernel parity verified at HEAD"* — it reads the **committed** tree. A re-run after the concurrent
edit to `scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js` became visible in the working tree
(` M scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js`) still exits 0 with identical output. That green is
therefore **not** evidence about site 2's uncommitted four-copy anchor state; it only says HEAD was
consistent. The anchor is not out of sync as far as `--check` can see, and in any case is not mine.
